_note: The MoE estate the expert population is placed in: node domains, tenants, policy domains and grants. Read corpus/state/README.md first.
_provenance: Assembled 2026-08-26 from spike_tenants (crates/orbweaver-object/src/bin/spike_tenants.rs) and spike_experts. Those two fixtures are the only pair among D026 section 1's five whose populations overlap, and they disagreed three ways; see README 'Measured 2026-08-26'. Restructured 2026-08-27 when the node-namespace question D028 section 4 M3 requires an answer to got one: TWO DOMAINS, not one vocabulary. The first version of this file listed the union of both under a single 'nodes' key, which is the one-domain answer written down as if it were bookkeeping.

node_domains._why: D028 section 4 M3 asks whether gpu-eu-1 and gpu-04 are one domain spelled twice or two domains. They are two, and the difference is mechanical rather than a matter of taste -- see corpus/state/README.md, 'The two node domains'. A node name is therefore NOT a workspace-wide identifier: which domain it belongs to is part of what it means, and a reader that resolves one against the other is asking a question neither domain can answer.

declared_estate._authority: the operator, out of band -- TenantService::declare_node. The contract declares no member for it.
declared_estate._default_deny: PolicyDomain::check_residency REFUSES a name not listed here. Membership has to be decidable or the refusal is not one.
declared_estate._undeclared_probe_note: Named so a residency check can be shown refusing default-deny. It is deliberately NOT in nodes above, and a loader that binds it has a defect.

reported_placement._authority: the expert itself, in-band -- moe::Capability.placement_node, a string member of corpus/golden/22-moe-control-plane.idl written by the expert about itself in register_expert and heartbeat.
reported_placement._note: Stored verbatim in the offer store and queried by the trader as an opaque value (placement_node == 'node-a', ORDER BY placement_node). No layer validates it, and no layer may: a set whose membership is decided by the thing being admitted is not a closed set. This list is the vocabulary THIS SEED uses, so a typo in an offer is catchable -- it is not an admission list, and adding a name to it grants nothing.

nodes.name: node-a
nodes._from: the trading fixture's placement_node, and every offer in moe-experts.json

reported_placement._two_deployments_note: node-a and gpu-04 are two deployments, not two spellings of one. Nothing states they are the same machines and nothing needs to; within this domain a name is whatever the expert reporting it says.

_capability_vocabulary_note: math, code and vision are the three capability words the MoE fixtures use. vision appears here in NO tenant's capability list and in NO grant, on purpose: spike_tenants asserts authorize('svc-acme','vision') is false, and that assertion is only meaningful while nobody has granted it. spike_experts meanwhile registers expert-vision as a pinned, Resident expert. The two are not in contradiction -- they are two worlds, and README's 'The two worlds vision lives in' says which is which. What was wrong was never the values; it was that no document said they were different worlds.
_ungranted_capability_note: The capability that must stay in the vocabulary and out of every grant, so spike_tenants' '...and only for what was granted' is refusing something. Stated rather than inferred: a reader that inferred it from 'whatever happens to be ungranted' would go quiet the day a grant was added, which is precisely when it should speak.
